title: E9 simulation readiness checkpoint form A
instructions: This protected readiness checkpoint is not the full mock. Apply the reported two-section timing, independent-work rules and composition protocol without inventing unconfirmed item counts.

parts.prompt: Which setup most faithfully protects the reported test structure?

options.text: Use one flexible 120-minute clock and move time freely between sections.
Run Section 1 for 90 minutes, stop it, then begin a separate 30-minute composition clock under the same no-help conditions.
Complete both sections untimed, then estimate how long they took.
Practise only the stronger section so the score looks more stable.

choice_rationales.A: Pooling time changes the reported boundaries.
choice_rationales.B: This preserves both section limits and consistent independent conditions.
choice_rationales.C: An untimed run does not test pacing.
choice_rationales.D: Omitting a section makes the evidence incomplete.

parts.hint: Protected checkpoint: no hint is available.
parts.correct_explanation: A valid rehearsal reproduces the separate 90-minute and 30-minute boundaries.

parts.prompt: Forty minutes remain in Section 1, but both reading passages are unseen and several earlier answers are flagged. What is the safest decision?

options.text: Continue polishing the first flagged vocabulary item until certain.
Move to reading, divide a workable reserve across both passages and keep a short final buffer for the most useful flagged returns.
Skip both passages and use the remaining time to count completed questions.
Ask someone which flagged answers should be changed.

choice_rationales.A: One uncertain item must not consume unsampled major tasks.
choice_rationales.B: This restores whole-section coverage while preserving a bounded review opportunity.
choice_rationales.C: Skipping reading invalidates the complete rehearsal.

parts.hint: Protected checkpoint: no hint is available.
parts.correct_explanation: Coverage of both passages outranks unlimited work on already sampled items.

parts.prompt: At the start of the 30-minute composition section, which sequence best protects a complete response?

options.text: Begin drafting immediately, discover the task requirements halfway through and edit only if time remains.
Use a bounded opening period to decode the prompt and make a compact plan, protect most time for drafting, then stop drafting with a short revision buffer still available.
Spend half the section searching for an impressive opening sentence.
Write several unrelated introductions and choose one at the end.

choice_rationales.A: Unplanned drafting risks missing a prompt requirement.
choice_rationales.B: The sequence protects task control, completion and final revision within the fixed clock.
choice_rationales.C: An opening cannot consume the time needed for the whole response.
choice_rationales.D: Multiple discarded openings reduce completion time without improving coverage.

parts.hint: Protected checkpoint: no hint is available.
parts.correct_explanation: The composition clock needs distinct planning, drafting and revision phases without rigid false precision.

parts.prompt: A genuine power failure closes the device during Section 1. Which recovery record best preserves cautious interpretation?

options.text: Restart from a fresh form after discussing difficult questions with a friend.
Record the stop and restart times, resume the same saved attempt without materials or discussion, and retain the disruption note with the result.
Delete the interruption from the record because it was accidental.
Use the interruption to look up every flagged answer.

choice_rationales.A: Discussion changes the evidence and a new form breaks continuity.
choice_rationales.B: This distinguishes traceable loss of access from assistance.

parts.hint: Protected checkpoint: no hint is available.
parts.correct_explanation: A technical interruption should be documented precisely and recovered without added help.

parts.prompt: Which post-simulation action produces the strongest next evidence?

options.text: Memorise the exposed answers and repeat the identical form tomorrow.
Treat the total as a guaranteed scholarship-admission prediction.
Classify errors by strand and cause, practise fresh material, then later use a matched unseen form under the same protocol.
Ignore strand results and keep only the overall percentage.

choice_rationales.A: Immediate identical repetition mainly measures recall.
choice_rationales.B: The internal form is not validated as an admission predictor.
choice_rationales.C: This links diagnosis, remediation and a cleaner transfer measure.

parts.hint: Protected checkpoint: no hint is available.
parts.correct_explanation: Fresh matched evidence after targeted practice is stronger than exposed-item repetition.
